subject: English
passage: The eucalyptus tree originated in Australia, where the marsupial Petauroides volans feeds on its leaves. In 1850, eucalyptus trees were brought to California, thousands of miles from any P. volans. But coevolutionary relationships between herbivores and their host plants can endure across vast distances and extended periods. Around 1995, P. volans was accidentally introduced to coastal California near where ecologist Nia Foster and her team had been studying eucalyptus growth patterns. Within eighteen months, 89 percent of the trees showed evidence of P. volans feeding damage.
prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the third sentence in the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It describes the research question that Foster and her team were attempting to answer through their eucalyptus studies.
choices.B: It presents a generalization that is exemplified by the discussion of the eucalyptus trees and P. volans.
choices.C: It explains the mechanism by which the organisms mentioned were able to colonize new environments.
choices.D: It proposes an alternative interpretation of the results obtained by Foster and her team.

explanation: Choice B is the best answer because it most accurately describes the function of the third sentence within the overall structure of the text. The third sentence makes a generalization, asserting that coevolutionary relationships between herbivores and host plants can endure across great expanses of distance and time. This generalization is exemplified by the text's discussion of the relationship between eucalyptus trees and P. volans. When eucalyptus trees were brought to California in 1850, no P. volans were present, so the relationship between the trees and the marsupials that exists in their native Australia was disrupted. When the marsupials were introduced to California more than 140 years later, however, they quickly damaged eucalyptus trees, illustrating the generalization that relationships between herbivores and host plants "can endure across vast distances and extended periods."
